results.title: PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) highlighted as a cheap big‑cap stock linked to Boy Thohir
results.body: The article spotlights PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) as a low‑priced big‑cap stock associated with Garibaldi “Boy” Thohir. It notes a trailing‑twelve‑months PE of 7.6× and a closing price of Rp 2,600 on 25 September 2026, with the share up 1.5% that day but down 1.5% over the prior week and 1.1% over the month, while YTD performance rose 43.6%. Financially, ADRO reported H1‑2026 revenue of US$999 million (+16.5% YoY), EBITDA of US$491 million (+56.8% YoY) and net profit of US$309 million (+76.9% YoY). The article also records a foreign net‑sell of Rp 78.3 billion during the week of 21‑25 September 2026 and identifies Garibaldi Thohir, Christian Ariano Rachmat, Michael WP Soeryadjaya and Arini Saraswaty Subianto as the individual beneficial owners of ADRO.

results.title: Foreign investors net sold Rp 4.39 trillion this week, with banks leading the top‑selling stocks
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 4.39 trillion across the market during the week ending 26/9/2026, contributing to the IHSG’s 3.09% decline to 6,241.89 points. The ten most net‑sold stocks were PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) Rp 1.1 trillion, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) Rp 676.34 billion, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) Rp 597.42 billion, PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) Rp 478.55 billion, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) Rp 213.79 billion, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) Rp 159.15 billion, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) Rp 125.58 billion, PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) Rp 96.45 billion, PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) Rp 74.93 billion and PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) Rp 72.91 billion.

results.title: Popular news roundup: Andy Hakim’s stake in PT Guna Timur Raya Tbk (TRUK), PT NexAI Digital Infrastruktur Tbk (MGLV)’s loan facility, PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA)’s 22.8% revenue growth, PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET)’s digital infrastructure expansion, and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Arkora Hydro Tbk (ARKO) competing for green power supply to Singapore
results.body: The article compiles the day’s most popular financial news, covering several corporate actions. Hakimson Growth Capital bought 5 % (21.75 million shares) of PT Guna Timur Raya Tbk (TRUK) at Rp 428 per share, a total of about Rp 9.3 billion, well below the Rp 1,420 closing price on 18 September 2026. PT NexAI Digital Infrastruktur Tbk (MGLV) secured a loan facility from PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) for its subsidiaries PT Nextier Askara Center (NAC) and PT Nextier GenAI Center (NGC) with a maximum commitment of Rp 4,125 trillion within an overall facility of Rp 10.75 trillion. PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) posted a 22.8 % year‑on‑year revenue increase to US$81.2 million in the first half of 2026, PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET) is expanding its digital infrastructure business, and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Arkora Hydro Tbk (ARKO) are competing to supply green electricity to Singapore from the Batam‑Bintan islands.

results.title: ADRO, MEDC, and ARKO Compete for Green Power Export to Singapore
results.body: The three issuers PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Arkora Hydro Tbk (ARKO) are competing to become Singapore’s green electricity supplier from the Batam‑Bintan islands. ADRO, through its subsidiary Adaro Solar International, has secured a 0.4 GW allocation from the Singapore regulator and plans a US$3.2 billion capital expenditure for the project. MEDC, via the Pacific Medco Solar Energy consortium with Grup Salim, obtained conditional approval for 600 MW within a 2 GWp Batam solar PV project. ARKO’s subsidiary Endorshine Energy Solutions received US$9.8 million financing from PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur for a commercial PLTS project, positioning ARKO as a potential dark‑horse contender.

results.title: IHSG projected to weaken on 24 Sept; BNI Sekuritas recommends six stocks
results.body: BNI Sekuritas' head of retail research, Fanny Suherman, expects the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) to face another correction on 24 Sept, with support around 6,320‑6,340 and resistance near 6,420‑6,440 after the index closed up 1.56% at 6,374.91 on 23 Sept amid a net foreign sell of Rp 468 billion. The brokerage issued speculative‑buy recommendations for six stocks: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) with entry 1,450‑1,465, stop‑loss below 1,450 and target 1,480‑1,500; PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) entry 2,570‑2,600, stop‑loss below 2,570, target 2,620‑2,660; PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG) entry 1,940‑1,980, stop‑loss below 1,940, target 2,030‑2,060; PT MNC Tourism Indonesia Tbk (KPIG) entry 55, stop‑loss below 54, target 57‑60; PT Astrindo Nusantara Infrastruktur Tbk (BIPI) entry 147‑150, stop‑loss below 146, target 155‑160; and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) entry 935‑960, stop‑loss below 920, target 980‑1,020. The recommendations come as foreign investors sold BBRI, BMRI, TLKM, ISAT and ADRO, with ADRO also appearing among the picks. BNI Sekuritas positions these six stocks as speculative opportunities ahead of the anticipated IHSG pull‑back.

results.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) lead foreign net sell list as IHSG rebounds.
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rebounded on Wednesday, closing at 6,374.91, up 97.86 points (1.56%). Despite the market gain, foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp461.35 billion across the market, with 448 stocks advancing, 186 declining and 159 unchanged. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net sell were PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) (Rp187.64 bn), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) (Rp128.73 bn), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) (Rp124.67 bn), PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) (Rp66.49 bn), PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) (Rp45.77 bn), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) (Rp35.30 bn), PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) (Rp31.01 bn), PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) (Rp28.87 bn), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) (Rp28.27 bn), and PT AKR Corporindo Tbk (AKRA) (Rp20.33 bn). Total trading volume reached 36.09 billion shares with a transaction value of Rp12.54 trillion.

results.title: BNI Sekuritas forecasts short-term IHSG rebound and recommends six stocks
results.body: BNI Sekuritas' Head of Retail, Fanny Suherman, forecasts a short-term technical rebound for Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) to the 6,300-6,320 range, noting support at 6,200-6,220 and resistance at 6,300-6,320, and warning that failure to break above 6,320 may lead to a correction toward 5,850-6,100, after the index closed at 6,277.04 on 22 September 2026. The index fell 1.69% with a net foreign sell of Rp 672 billion, driven by heavy sales of BBRI, TINS, BBCA, BMRI and TPIA. BNI Sekuritas recommends six stocks: PT Intermedia Capital Tbk (MDIA) – speculative buy at Rp 175‑Rp 177, target Rp 184‑Rp 190; PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) – speculative buy at Rp 180‑Rp 184, target Rp 188‑Rp 190; PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) – speculative buy at Rp 970‑Rp 980, target Rp 1,015‑Rp 1,025. It also advises PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) – speculative buy at Rp 2,800‑Rp 2,830, target Rp 2,870‑Rp 2,940; PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET) – buy on weakness at Rp 304‑Rp 316, target Rp 320‑Rp 330; and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) – buy on weakness at Rp 2,580‑Rp 2,610, target Rp 2,630‑Rp 2,680.

results.title: Foreign investors net sold Rp 510.07 bn of Indonesian stocks, led by PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI)
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 510.07 bn on Monday, sending the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) down 0.88% to 6,384.72 points. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net outflows were PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) (Rp 140.61 bn), PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) (Rp 139.93 bn), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) (Rp 131.34 bn), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) (Rp 114.62 bn), PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) (Rp 32.42 bn), PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) (Rp 26.38 bn), PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) (Rp 25.81 bn), PT Alamtri Resoruces Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) (Rp 22.32 bn), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) (Rp 21.98 bn), and PT Energi Mega Persada Tbk (ENRG) (Rp 16.65 bn). Overall market activity was high, with 26.78 billion shares traded for a total value of Rp 11.77 trillion. Sectorally, infrastructure fell 1.38% while transport rose 0.55%, health gained 0.21% and property remained flat.

results.title: Foreign investors sell shares of major banks and Prajogo‑linked stocks
results.body: Foreign investors net sold shares of major banks and Prajogo‑linked stocks during the week of 14–18 September 2026. The largest net sell was PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) with Rp798 billion, followed by PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) with Rp443.2 billion, PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) with Rp193.2 billion, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) with Rp189.9 billion, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) with Rp166.3 billion, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) with Rp132.6 billion, PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) with Rp95 billion, PT Timah Tbk (TINS) with Rp47.7 billion, PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) with Rp45 billion and PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) with Rp44.6 billion. Foreign investors’ net sell for the week totaled Rp1.84 trillion, contributing to a 1.53% decline in the IHSG to 6,441,159 and a 1.58% drop in market capitalization to Rp11,266 trillion, while average daily transaction value, frequency and volume fell 6.95%, 14.73% and 20.71% respectively. The sell‑off coincided with the Federal Reserve’s 25‑basis‑point rate hike to a target range of 3.75‑4% on 16 September 2026 and analysts’ view that further US rate increases may prompt Bank Indonesia to consider similar moves.

results.title: Summary of stock recommendations for 8 September 2026 from seven Indonesian securities firms.
results.body: The article summarizes stock recommendations issued by seven Indonesian securities firms for Tuesday, 8 September 2026, following a 0.25% decline in the IHSG to 6,619 on Monday. The index fell amid weakness in financial, raw material, and technology sectors, which dropped 0.75%, 0.71%, and 0.61% respectively, with trading volume of 37.05 billion shares worth Rp13.73 trillion. The brokers recommended a total of 24 stocks: IMPC, TINS, KOTA from BRI Danareksa Sekuritas; SSIA, ADRO, BBRI, ERAA, COCO, COIN from BNI Sekuritas; HMSP, MDIA from Phillip Sekuritas; HRUM, INKP, MDKA, TPIA from MNC Sekuritas; HMSP, INDF, BTPS, TAPG, CMRY, BUMI from CGS International Sekuritas; INDF, INKP, AKRA, BFIN, MNCN from Phintraco Sekuritas; and ADRO, DEWA, INKP from Mirae Asset Sekuritas. Several stocks, including HMSP, INKP, ADRO, and INDF, were recommended by multiple firms.

results.title: Pilarmas Investindo Sekuritas recommends ADRO, AMRT and SSMS as IHSG faces limited correction
results.body: The article forecasts that the Indonesian composite index (IHSG) will experience limited downside, with support around 6,600 and resistance near 6,710 after closing at 6,636 on September 4, 2026. Pilarmas Investindo Sekuritas points to technical signals and macro conditions—including US‑Iran tensions, OPEC+ production stance and a rise in the 10‑year SBN yield to 7.23% before easing to about 7.1%—as background for its outlook. The brokerage recommends trading the stocks ADRO, AMRT and SSMS on Monday, September 7, 2026.

results.title: Foreign investors heavily buy big bank stocks PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk in the past week.
results.body: The article reports that foreign investors returned to Indonesia’s banking sector last week, posting the largest net purchases in the market for the three big banks. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk recorded a net buy of Rp 1.41 trillion, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk Rp 1.20 trillion and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk Rp 1.01 trillion, together accounting for about Rp 3.62 trillion of foreign inflows, while PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk added Rp 261.39 billion. Other heavily bought stocks included PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp 238.84 billion), PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (Rp 168.05 billion), PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (Rp 147.58 billion), PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk (Rp 126.94 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (Rp 93.49 billion) and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (Rp 84.23 billion). Foreign investors sold PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (Rp 485.66 billion), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (Rp 337.42 billion), PT Indosat Tbk (Rp 225.62 billion), PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (Rp 173 billion), PT Petrosea Tbk (Rp 162.7 billion), PT Astra International Tbk (Rp 150.28 billion), PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (Rp 129.03 billion), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (Rp 126.97 billion), PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (Rp 121.57 billion) and PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk (Rp 109.91 billion), contributing to a total foreign net buy of Rp 1.85 trillion and supporting a 1.82 % weekly rise in the IHSG index, which closed at 6,636.47, down 31.4 points (0.47 %) on Friday.

results.title: IHSG Still Has Opportunity to Strengthen on Monday (7/9), Here Are Analyst-Recommended Stocks
results.body: The article discusses the potential for the Indonesian Composite Index (IHSG) to strengthen on Monday, 7 September 2026, after a 0.47% decline to 6,636 on Friday, 4 September 2026, and a weekly gain of 1.82%. Analyst William Hartanto projects the index to trade between 6,612 and 6,704 on Monday, citing a gap at 6,704 formed on 13 May 2026 and the index remaining above the 5‑period moving average as evidence of a strong uptrend. He recommends buying PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) with a target price of Rp 2,800–Rp 2,820 per share and PT Baramulti Suksessarana Tbk (BSSR) with a target price of Rp 5,000 per share.

results.title: Stock Market Gains, Simas Syariah Unggulan Mutual Fund Posts 10.28% Return in August
results.body: Sinarmas Asset Management’s Simas Syariah Unggulan fund posted a 10.28% month‑on‑month return in August 2026, far above the average reksadana saham return of 3.60% and the IHSG index gain of 4.64% in the same period. The fund’s outperformance was driven by basic materials and consumer non‑cyclical sector strength and its top holdings of Bank Jabar Banten Syariah (18.57%), Aneka Tambang (18%), Dharma Satya Nusantara (15.01%), Archi Indonesia (12.20%) and Japfa Comfeed Indonesia (11.49%). Batavia Prosperindo Asset Management’s Batavia Dana Saham Syariah fund delivered a 6.04% month‑on‑month return, supported by energy, basic materials and infrastructure exposure, with its largest positions in Aneka Tambang (6.47%), Alamtri Resources Indonesia (5.10%), Kalbe Farma (4.29%), Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur (4.11%) and Indofood Sukses Makmur (3.73%). Both managers outlined sector‑focused strategies for the next period, with Batavia planning to increase energy exposure and Sinarmas intending to use artificial intelligence to enhance asset allocation.

results.title: IHSG and Asian Exchanges Cheerful This Morning
results.body: The Jakarta Stock Exchange (IHSG) opened higher on Friday, September 4, 2026, gaining 27.8 points (0.42%) to 6,695 as Asian markets such as KOSDAQ, Hang Seng, KOSPI, Shenzhen Composite, CSI 300, Straits Times, Shanghai Composite, NIKKEI 225 and TW Weighted Index also rose in green zones. The rally was supported by a net foreign purchase of Rp1.07 trillion, a strong rupiah at Rp17,660 per USD, and bullish technical levels with the index breaking resistance at 6,650 and targeting 6,724 while holding support near 6,550. Brokers highlighted several stocks as top picks: BRI Danareksa recommended BBCA, LSIP and ARCI; Phintraco listed JPFA, PANI, CPIN, ANTM and ARCI; CGS International suggested ADMR, AADI, ADRO, SMGR, BMRI and MDKA; and Panin Sekuritas favored BDMN, AALI and SMDR. Analysts noted that continued foreign buying, commodity price gains and a dovish Fed outlook could sustain the market, though short‑term profit‑taking ahead of the weekend remains a risk.

results.title: Foreign Investors Net Buy Rp1.07 Trillion, Lifting IHSG 1.09% as Jumbo Banks Lead Inflows
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net buy of Rp1.07 trillion in the Indonesian stock market on Thursday, September 3, 2026, propelling the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) up 1.09% to 6,667.89. The four jumbo banks — Bank Mandiri, Bank Central Asia, Bank Negara Indonesia, and Bank Rakyat Indonesia — accounted for approximately Rp801 billion, or 75% of total foreign net buying. Other notable foreign purchases included Charoen Pokphand Indonesia, Aneka Tambang, Alamtri Resources Indonesia, and Chandra Asri Pacific. On the sell side, Buana Lintas Lautan, Bumi Resources, and Petrosea topped the net sell list.

results.title: Energy Stock Rally Targets ADRO and BUMI
results.body: Energy stocks are rallying, with ADRO and BUMI among the companies targeted by the surge. The IDX Energy index rose 12.6% in the past month and gained 1.36% on 3 September 2026, outpacing the broader market. Analysts say the rally is driven by improving earnings prospects, stronger valuations, and investor funds returning to commodity stocks with solid fundamentals, rather than commodity price euphoria alone, and they expect the energy sector to remain a support for the IHSG until the end of 2026. The next phase will focus on stock picking, favoring companies with low production costs, healthy balance sheets, strong cash flows, large reserves, and the ability to maintain production volumes.

results.title: Batavia Dana Saham Syariah posts a 6.04% return in August, highlighting data center infrastructure stocks
results.body: The article reports that Batavia Dana Saham Syariah, a Sharia‑compliant equity fund managed by Batavia Prosperindo Asset Management, delivered a 6.04% month‑on‑month return in August 2026. This outperformed the average mutual‑fund equity return of 3.60% for the same period and was driven by the fund’s largest active weight in the infrastructure sector, particularly stocks linked to data‑center development. The portfolio’s top holdings included Aneka Tambang (6.47%), Alamtri Resources Indonesia (5.10%), Kalbe Farma (4.29%), Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur (4.11%) and Indofood Sukses Makmur (3.73%). The manager also indicated plans to increase exposure to the energy sector, citing an El‑Niño view as a catalyst for future adjustments.

results.title: Energy sector stays a market primadona as analysts recommend PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk and PT Bukit Asam Tbk
results.body: The IDX Energy index rose 1.36% to 3,364.14 on 3 September 2026, marking a 14.16% gain for the month and underscoring the sector’s continued strength. Analysts Hendra Wardana and Sukarno Alatas attribute the momentum to improving fundamentals, commodity price support, and production recovery in the second half of 2026. Wardana recommends PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk, an emiten, as a trading buy with a target price of Rp2,860 per share. He also recommends PT Bukit Asam Tbk, an emiten, as a trading buy with a target price of Rp3,000 per share.

results.title: Foreign investors net buy Rp1 trillion, collectively snapping up PT Bank Mandiri Tbk and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk shares
results.body: Foreign investors net bought about Rp1 trillion in Indonesian equities on Thursday, with state‑owned banks PT Bank Mandiri Tbk and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk leading the inflows. The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 1.09% at 6,667.89 points on a trading volume of 40.79 billion shares and total transaction value of Rp18.64 trillion. PT Bank Mandiri Tbk recorded the largest net foreign purchase of Rp471.38 billion (foreign transaction value Rp1.04 trillion), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk ranked seventh with a net foreign buy of Rp87.40 billion (total foreign transaction Rp176.42 billion), while PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk, PT Aneka Tambang Tbk, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk, PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk, PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk, PT Astra International Tbk and PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk each posted net foreign buys ranging from Rp57.20 billion to Rp207.10 billion. The inflows came amid positive domestic sentiment after the Bank Indonesia governor’s emphasis on economic stability, despite lingering global geopolitical tensions.
